sources.title: Human History Map: Jordan index and border features
sources.note: Own-project factual-data exception. Index 1938 to null. All seven features decoded in identity.json; 1938 fragmentary multipolygon excludes an Amman point, later historical polygons exclude tested West Bank towns and Aqaba point, modern outline includes Aqaba. Point probes documented separately. Shapes do not establish actual sovereignty, control or future borders.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: Jordan recognition and diplomatic history
sources.note: Direct original government history. British mandate context, independence declared 25 May 1946, US recognition 31 January 1949 and diplomatic relations 18 February 1949. These dates are distinct.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Country Profile, Jordan, September 2006
sources.note: Original 27-page PDF directly read. Printed pages 3 to 5: Transjordan under British supervision, 1950 annexation after 1948 war, 1967 Israeli occupation, 1970 fighting and 1971 expulsion of guerrillas, 1988 legal/administrative disengagement. Avoided disputed recognition count and dated demographic claims. Limited historical use, not a current-country source.

sources.title: Jordanian House of Representatives: Arabic constitution
sources.note: Direct Arabic text, Articles 1, 20, 25, 26, 35 and 36. Current amended constitution; no claim this HTML is an original 1952 facsimile. Article 20 excerpt exact التعليم الأساسي إلزامي للأردنيين. Official English Ministry of Justice version independently matched.

sources.title: Jordanian Ministry of Justice: Constitutional rights and duties
sources.note: Direct institutional English text introduces the 1952 constitution and amendments. Article 20 begins Elementary education shall be compulsory for Jordanians, followed by free government schooling. Arabic and translation grouped as one constitutional work for conservative budgeting. Unrelated duplicated/mistranslated Article 10 on this webpage not used.

sources.title: United Nations: Israel-Jordan peace treaty, 26 October 1994
sources.note: Direct/indexed original treaty deposited with UN, document A/50/73 and S/1995/83. Articles 1 to 3 and 6, mutual recognition, boundary and water arrangements. Article 3 preserves status of territories under Israeli military control in 1967; no inference that Palestinian questions were settled.

sources.title: Congressional Research Service: Jordan, Background and US Relations, 8 January 2026
sources.note: Direct January 8, 2026 edition. Royal family, political system, regional relationships and April 2025 Muslim Brotherhood ban. The associated Islamic Action Front is not conflated with the banned organization. Its 2024 seats and January 2026 legal status are dated, not assumed permanently current. All versions of this report treated as one work.

sources.title: Smithsonian Museum Conservation Institute: Ain Ghazal statues
sources.note: Direct conservation account. Fragile contents blocklifted in 1985, foil/foam/crate, seven-year lab work, two standing figures and three two-headed busts, 1996 to 1997 exhibition and return to Jordan. Scholarly paper indicates initial discovery of second cache in 1984, so draft says recovered in 1985, not discovered then. Approximate ancient dates omitted because site summaries use uncalibrated chronology.

sources.title: UNESCO Courier: SESAME, scientific excellence in the Middle East
sources.note: Direct 11 October 2018 article by Anoud Al-Zoubi. Centre opened in Allan 16 May 2017; synchrotron described as powerful high-precision research microscope; eight members and scientific collaboration. Medical/material/archaeology capabilities described as research uses, not cures or political reconciliation proven.

sources.title: UNESCO: Al-Mansaf in Jordan, a festive banquet and its social meanings
sources.note: Full indexed original UNESCO listing read, 2022 inscription. Meat and yogurt sauce with bread/rice/bulgur, social preparation, five to seven around a platter, changing utensil habits, family and institute teaching. No exclusive culinary-origin claim. No song quoted.

sources.title: UNICEF Jordan: Education, including 2025 programme results
sources.note: Direct current programme page, specific 2025 results: 20,000 children receiving Arabic/math support in 114 Makani centres; 4,617 camp children in Reading Recovery Programme. General access statistics without clear observation year avoided. Lists poverty, disability and displacement barriers.

sources.title: WHO: Refugee and migrant health system review, Jordan, 24 June 2024
sources.note: Direct official review overview. Subsidized essential health services for vulnerable populations, joint WHO/Ministry review and service-delivery challenges. No universal free-care or current refugee population claim; overview dates for Syrian onset are not copied.

sources.title: WHO Eastern Mediterranean: Jordan concludes Syrian Crisis Response Project
sources.note: Full indexed original report dated 24 March 2025 read; direct opening failed. Vaccine storage in Irbid, solar-powered national warehouse, four cold rooms and 380 refrigerators, 24 refrigerated trucks. Project benefits refugees and host communities; no all-children coverage assertion.

sources.title: UNICEF: Jordan school water and sanitation support, 31 August 2020
sources.note: Direct press release, Samir Al-Refai School in Amman: drinking stations, greywater system for toilets, soap, 46-school handwashing repair programme during COVID-19 reopening. Old national one-in-three statistic omitted as not current.

sources.title: UNICEF Jordan: Water, sanitation and hygiene, including 2025 results
sources.note: Direct programme page. 2025 results: 35 schools in Irbid/Mafraq with greywater treatment/reuse and nearly 40,000 students; 2,300 children in Climate Action Clubs. Intermittent water and conservation context. Avoided treating renewable-resource volume as household allocation or stating all homes receive weekly supply.

sources.title: UNICEF: A door that locks, private latrines in Azraq camp, 3 August 2026
sources.note: Direct dated account by AbelMajid El-Noaimi. Khadija and seven children, communal unlit toilets, private household latrine and drainage/sewage connection. Family fled Syria in 2014. Children names/details kept limited; no quoted testimony and no medical outcome inference. Camp-specific, not representative of all Jordanian homes.

proposedOverrides.name: Jordan
proposedOverrides.summary: Jordan: from British-protected Transjordan to an independent kingdom, with regional diplomacy, scientific cooperation, shared meals and changing schools, healthcare and sanitation.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One coherent modern-polity card across the imported 1938 to present record, with pre-independence Transjordan explicitly identified. No merging with ancient Nabataean or other regional societies.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Seven features decoded. 1938 to 1945 multipolygon bbox [35.656556565565666,29.42072075930205,36.72216722167224,32.71921009537672], fragmentary and excludes tested Amman coordinate [35.93,31.95]. Historical 1945 to 2020 polygons extend east but do not contain tested Jenin, Nablus or East Jerusalem points, thus cannot show Jordanian West Bank administration accurately. Tested Aqaba coordinate is also absent before modern replacement. 2020 to 2100 modern polygon bbox [34.923,29.197,39.195,33.379] includes Amman and Aqaba. All raw coordinates saved; no geometry correction attempted.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: 1938 is atlas coverage, 25 May 1946 independence declaration, 1950 West Bank annexation, 1967 occupation by Israel, 1970 to 1971 internal conflict, 1988 disengagement, 1994 peace treaty, 1999 succession. Contemporary policy claims are anchored to January 2026 CRS and dated 2025/2026 programme evidence.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Exact Arabic Article 20 opening, four words, compared with Ministry of Justice English rendering of eight words. Current official text, not a scan of an original enactment; bilingual constitutional sources budgeted as one work.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceBoundaries: Historical LOC profile used only for past events, not present population or politics. Modern discovery/conservation of Neolithic objects is not treated as their creation by the kingdom. Refugee camp sanitation and selected-school greywater projects remain local examples. All research browser-free.
